about: Five questions about mandi.db (sample data, not real prices). Each has a truth query written and checked by hand. Question 4 is the AND/OR trap.

questions.question: Which city had the cheapest onions on day 3?
questions.truth_sql: SELECT city FROM daily_prices WHERE vegetable = 'onion' AND day = 3 ORDER BY price_rs_per_kg ASC LIMIT 1

questions.question: What was the average brinjal price in Indore over the ten days, in rupees per kg?
questions.truth_sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(price_rs_per_kg), 2) FROM daily_prices WHERE vegetable = 'brinjal' AND city = 'Indore'

questions.question: On which day did Pune get the most potato arrivals?
questions.truth_sql: SELECT day FROM daily_prices WHERE vegetable = 'potato' AND city = 'Pune' ORDER BY arrivals_quintals DESC LIMIT 1

questions.question: How many quintals of onions reached Nashik and Pune on day 3, taken together?
questions.trap: In English we say 'Nashik and Pune', but in SQL it is city = 'Nashik' OR city = 'Pune'. SQL applies AND before OR, so without brackets around the OR part every Pune row (all days, all vegetables) leaks into the sum.
questions.trap_sql: SELECT SUM(arrivals_quintals) FROM daily_prices WHERE vegetable = 'onion' AND day = 3 AND city = 'Nashik' OR city = 'Pune'
questions.truth_sql: SELECT SUM(arrivals_quintals) FROM daily_prices WHERE vegetable = 'onion' AND day = 3 AND (city = 'Nashik' OR city = 'Pune')

questions.question: By what percent did the tomato price in Pune rise from day 1 to day 10?
questions.truth_sql: SELECT ROUND((d10.price_rs_per_kg - d1.price_rs_per_kg) * 100.0 / d1.price_rs_per_kg, 2) FROM daily_prices AS d1 JOIN daily_prices AS d10 ON d10.vegetable = d1.vegetable AND d10.city = d1.city WHERE d1.vegetable = 'tomato' AND d1.city = 'Pune' AND d1.day = 1 AND d10.day = 10
